nodes.summary: Suppose $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ has an essential isolated singularity at $c \in \mathbb{C}$. Then there is at most one $w \in \mathbb{C}$ for which some $r > 0$ makes the set $\{z : 0 < |z - c| < r,\ f(z) = w\}$ finite; that is, with at most one exception, $f$ takes every complex value infinitely often on every punctured disc around $c$.
nodes.title: Great Picard theorem

nodes.summary: A function $f : \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ has an essential isolated singularity at $c \in \mathbb{C}$ when $f$ is holomorphic on some punctured disc $0 < |z - c| < r$ with $r > 0$, $f(z)$ has no finite limit as $z \to c$ with $z \ne c$, and $|f(z)|$ does not tend to $\infty$ as $z \to c$ with $z \ne c$.
nodes.title: Essential isolated singularity
